annotations.title: Read a North Carolina (NC) General Statutes section

description:
Full text of one North Carolina (NC) General Statutes section, by citation.

Use for "what does G.S. 14-72.1 say". Accepts any spelling — "14-72.1", "G.S. 14-72.1",
"§ 14-72.1". Returns catchline, body, history note, and when it was first enacted and
last amended. `as_of` gives the text observed on a past date; `pending` lists variants
enacted but not yet effective.

Carries `codified_through`, `session_laws_through` and a `legislation_note` naming any
enacted act that touches this section outside the codified text. An uncodified override
("Notwithstanding G.S. ...") is never codified, so it is reported regardless of the
watermark. PENDING BILLS ARE NOT COVERED — a ratified bill is not law and appears in
neither source, so an empty note is not evidence nothing passed.

`as_of` RESOLVES AGAINST OBSERVED VERSIONS, NOT EFFECTIVE DATES — it answers "what did
this database hold on that date", so it cannot reach text from before the first ingest
run. For "what took effect on 1 October" use recent_law_changes(source="effective").

Section-level only — ask for "20-141", not "20-141(j1)". The Rules of Evidence and of
Civil Procedure are each one statute (G.S. 8C-1, G.S. 1A-1) holding many rules; ask for a
rule as "8C-1, Rule 104" or "1A-1, Rule 12" (N.C. R. Evid. / N.C. R. Civ. P. forms work).
Asking for 8C-1 or 1A-1 itself lists the rules. For WHEN it changed use
amendment_history; for WHAT changed use diff_statute.

citation.description: One NC General Statutes SECTION, or one rule of the Rules of Evidence or Civil Procedure ("8C-1, Rule 104", "N.C. R. Civ. P. 12"). Any spelling works; subsections do not — ask for 20-141, not 20-141(j1), and 1A-1, Rule 12, not Rule 12(b)(6).
